description: Each Irish constituency's own date in the general elections of 1832-1880, read from B. M. Walker's printed tables. A general election's contests all carry the election's nominal date, which keeps them together as one election; this file adds the date Walker prints against each seat, shown in the contest panel as a note. It never changes a contest's date or which election it belongs to.

dateKinds.return: 1832-1868: Walker prints the official date of return (introduction, p. xii): the day the returning officer signed the writ returning the members, usually the day the poll closed and was declared. Shown as 'Date of return'.
dateKinds.election: 1874 and 1880: after the Ballot Act the official dates are when writs reached Westminster, so Walker takes the date of the election from newspapers (introduction, p. xii). Shown as 'Polling day' for a contest, 'Returned unopposed' for an unopposed return.

method: Read by eye from page renders of the private scan, one general election at a time, 2026-10-29; matched to Civgraph's contest files by constituency name (Walker's 'X county' is Civgraph's 'X' or 'County X'; Walker's 'Galway' is 'Galway Borough'). Page is Walker's printed page, where the seat's entry begins. Figures only: no text from the volume is reproduced.

records.why: Walker prints Mar. 20, the day before the dissolution of 21 March 1857, so probably a misprint; not shown until settled from another source
